claims.text: Replacing EAM references with a deep-learning interatomic potential will significantly improve reference–target phase-space overlap in high-entropy alloys near and above their melting points.
The proposed method applies to both solid and liquid states of multicomponent high-entropy materials.
High-entropy materials near melting exhibit rich configurational diversity.
The DNN reference should be trained directly on a representative set of ab initio liquid-state configurations.
The trained DNN potential should replace an empirical EAM potential as the reference in a thermodynamic-integration scheme such as TOR-TILD.
The applicable temperature range is approximately 0.9 Tm to Tm.
The method is applicable to multicomponent refractory high-entropy carbonitrides.
The method is applicable to tungsten-based high-entropy alloys.
A DNN potential can represent complex solid and liquid structures in a high-entropy Ti-Zr-Ta-Hf-Nb carbonitride.
The DNN reference more accurately represents the liquid energy landscape and complex atomic configurations than an EAM reference.
The machine-learned potential accurately captures energy fluctuations and diverse atomic arrangements in the ab initio liquid.
Capturing those fluctuations and arrangements enhances overlap between the reference and target phase spaces.
Enhanced phase-space overlap produces a smoother and more continuous thermodynamic-integration path.
The DNN reference will substantially reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM reference.
Reduced path mismatch will make the free-energy calculation more accurate and efficient.
Similar significant improvements have been observed in deep-learning models of related systems.
Traditional EAM references in TOR-TILD suffer from poor reference–target phase-space overlap because they insufficiently represent liquid configurations.
The intervention will be most effective for compositionally complex liquids very close to Tm and less effective for less complex alloys or temperatures far below melting.
The magnitude of mismatch reduction and its composition dependence are uncertain pending systematic benchmarking.
The hypothesis is falsified if the DNN reference fails to produce a statistically significant reduction in path mismatch relative to EAM or remains inconsistent with ab initio free-energy benchmarks.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis includes temperatures above Tm, whereas the stated initial-state example and applicable range are limited to 0.9–1.0 Tm and 0.9 Tm to Tm.
